easy.question: What makes a group of people a community?
options: They live in the same area and share common spaces
They all go to the same school
easy.answer: They live in the same area and share common spaces
easy.explanation: A community is formed by people who live in the same neighbourhood, share common places like markets and parks, and look out for each other.

easy.question: Which of these is a public place?
easy.explanation: A library is a public place because it is open for everyone to use. Drawing rooms, balconies and wardrobes are private spaces inside your home.

easy.question: Places like parks, playgrounds and bus stops that anyone can use are called ______ places.
easy.explanation: Public places are shared spaces that belong to everyone in the community. People can use them for walking, playing, waiting and reading.

easy.question: Name any three important places you would find in a community.
easy.answer: Schools, hospitals and markets are three important places found in a community.
easy.explanation: Every community has places that people depend on daily -- schools for learning, hospitals for health, and markets for buying essentials.

easy.question: Which of these should we NOT do in a public park?
options: Sit on a bench and read
easy.explanation: Public places belong to everyone. We should always use dustbins and keep parks clean so that all people can enjoy them.

medium.question: Why are public places important for the people in a community?
medium.answer: Public places are important because they serve common needs. Parks give people a place to exercise and relax, libraries provide books for reading, bus stops help people travel, and playgrounds let children play safely. Without these shared spaces, daily life would be much harder.
medium.explanation: Public places bring people together and provide essential services that individual homes cannot offer on their own.

medium.question: What problems can arise if a community does not have a hospital or clinic nearby?
medium.answer: If a community does not have a hospital or clinic, people who fall ill or get injured will have to travel far for treatment. In emergencies, this delay can be very dangerous. Even simple things like buying medicines or getting a check-up become difficult for everyone.
medium.explanation: Each important place in a community serves a specific need. When it is missing, people suffer, especially during urgent situations.

medium.question: Each place in a community is like a piece of a ______ puzzle -- take one away and the picture is incomplete.
medium.explanation: Just like every piece of a jigsaw puzzle is needed to complete the picture, every place in a community -- school, market, hospital -- plays an important role.

hard.question: Write four things you can do to keep public places in your neighbourhood clean and well-maintained.
hard.answer: 1. Always throw waste into a dustbin instead of on the ground. 2. Avoid scribbling or drawing on walls of public buildings. 3. Handle shared things like benches, swings and library books gently. 4. If you see litter, pick it up and put it in the bin, and encourage others to do the same.
hard.explanation: Public places belong to all of us. When everyone takes a little responsibility, these spaces stay clean, safe and enjoyable for the whole community.

easy.question: When is Van Mahotsav celebrated every year in India?
easy.explanation: Van Mahotsav, the Festival of Forests, is celebrated from 1st July to 7th July every year, during the monsoon season.

easy.question: Van Mahotsav is also called the Festival of ______.
easy.explanation: Van Mahotsav means Festival of Forests. People across India plant trees during this week to protect the environment and increase greenery.

easy.question: Which tool does a mason use to spread cement on bricks?
easy.explanation: A mason uses a trowel to spread and smooth cement while building or repairing walls.

easy.question: What is the work of a carpenter?
easy.answer: A carpenter crafts doors, windows and wooden furniture using tools like a saw, chisel and hammer.
easy.explanation: Carpenters are skilled workers who shape and join wood to make useful items for homes and offices.

easy.question: Which community helper keeps the streets and lanes clean?
easy.explanation: Sanitation workers clear garbage and sweep streets to keep our neighbourhood clean and healthy.

medium.question: How did a school near Bhopal celebrate Van Mahotsav? Mention any three activities.
medium.answer: The students swept the school ground, parents and the gardener dug pits for saplings, a local nursery owner donated neem and mango saplings, children watered the saplings, and the art teacher made name tags with students.
medium.explanation: Van Mahotsav celebrations involve the whole community working together. Each person contributes something to make the event a success.

medium.question: Why is Van Mahotsav held during the monsoon months?
options: Because it is a national holiday
Because the rainy season helps saplings grow
medium.answer: Because the rainy season helps saplings grow
medium.explanation: During the monsoon, the soil is soft and moist. Rain provides natural water to newly planted saplings, helping their roots spread easily.

hard.question: Why is every helper important in a community? Explain with examples of at least three community helpers and their work.
hard.answer: Every helper plays a vital role in keeping the community running smoothly. A mason builds and repairs walls so that our houses remain strong and safe. An electrician fixes wires, fans and lights, making sure we have electricity at home. A sanitation worker clears garbage and sweeps streets -- without them, dirt and disease would spread. If any one of these helpers stopped working, our daily life would be seriously affected. Each person's skill is needed by the community.
hard.explanation: No single person can do everything. Different helpers bring different skills, and together they keep the neighbourhood safe, clean and comfortable for all.

easy.question: Which tiny creature is a well-known example of teamwork in nature?
easy.explanation: Ants work in teams -- some find food, some carry it back, and some guard the nest. A single ant is small, but together they can carry objects much bigger than themselves.

easy.question: During Onam in Kerala, neighbours make a beautiful flower carpet called ______.
easy.explanation: Pookalam is a colourful flower arrangement made on the ground during Onam. Families contribute different flowers and create it together.

easy.question: During which festival in Punjab do families gather around a bonfire?
easy.explanation: Lohri is celebrated in Punjab on a cold January night. Families sit around a bonfire, toss peanuts and popcorn into the flames, and sing folk songs.

easy.question: What happens to banana leaves when they are buried in the soil?
easy.answer: When banana leaves are buried in the soil, they break down over time and turn into natural compost, which makes the earth richer for growing plants.
easy.explanation: Banana leaves decompose naturally and add nutrients to the soil, acting as a natural fertiliser.

medium.question: How did the people of Punsari village in Gujarat show the power of teamwork?
medium.answer: The villagers of Punsari decided to solve their problems together. They set up CCTV cameras for safety, installed solar street lights, started a village bus service for children, and built a water purification plant. Today Punsari is known across India as a model village.
medium.explanation: This real-life example proves that when a community works together, ordinary people can achieve extraordinary results.

medium.question: Why are festivals important for a community?
options: They give time off from work
They bring people together and strengthen bonds
They happen only in big cities
medium.answer: They bring people together and strengthen bonds
medium.explanation: Festivals bring neighbours together to share food, joy and traditions. This shared experience creates lasting memories and makes communities stronger.

hard.question: Give two examples from the chapter that show how teamwork helps people. What lesson do we learn from them?
hard.answer: Example 1: During Van Mahotsav, a school near Bhopal celebrated by dividing tasks among students, parents, the gardener, and the nursery owner. Everyone did their part -- sweeping, digging, planting and watering -- and the work was finished happily. Example 2: In Punsari village, Gujarat, the entire community came together to install solar lights, set up clean drinking water, and start a bus service. The village became a model for the whole country. The lesson is that when people work as a team, even big challenges can be solved quickly and effectively.
hard.explanation: Both examples show that no one person can do everything alone. When a community shares responsibility, tasks become lighter and results become greater.
